::: {#exm-two-state-chain}
#### A two-state weather chain

Each day is dry or wet.
A dry day is followed by a dry day with probability 0.9,
and a wet day is followed by a dry day with probability 0.5,
whatever the weather on earlier days.
So the daily weather is a [Markov chain](#def-markov-chain).

Let $\prob_{\text{dry}}$ be the probability that a day is dry.
For that probability to be the same the next day,

$$
\ba
\prob_{\text{dry}}
&= 0.9\, \prob_{\text{dry}} + 0.5\, (1 - \prob_{\text{dry}})
&& \text{(tomorrow is dry after a dry or a wet day)}\\
&= 0.5 + 0.4\, \prob_{\text{dry}}
&& \text{(collecting terms)},
\ea
$$

so $0.6\, \prob_{\text{dry}} = 0.5$
and $\prob_{\text{dry}} = 5/6$.
The [stationary distribution](#def-stationary-distribution)
is dry with probability $5/6$ and wet with probability $1/6$.
A simulated chain, started on a wet day,
spends about that fraction of its days dry:

```{r}
#| label: two-state-chain
#| code-fold: false
set.seed(7)
n_days <- 10000
dry <- logical(n_days)
for (t in seq(2, n_days)) {
  p_dry <- if (dry[t - 1]) 0.9 else 0.5
  dry[t] <- stats::runif(1) < p_dry
}
c(simulated = mean(dry), stationary = 5 / 6) |> round(3)
```
:::
